chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Musa ibn Ja'far al-Madaini from Ibrahim ibn Ismail ibn Dawud, who said:

I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) about fasting, and he said: 'Three days in the month: Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday.' I said: 'Indeed, our companions fast on Wednesday between two Thursdays.' He said: 'There is no harm in that, and there is no harm in fasting on Thursday between two Wednesdays.'

key_terms.الرِّضَا: Al-Rida (a specific title for Imam Ali al-Rida, peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended days for voluntary monthly fasting in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) identifies the first three days of the lunar month—Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday—as the optimal days for voluntary fasting, a practice rooted in the tradition of the Ahl al-Bayt. He simultaneously validates the widely practiced alternative of fasting on the Wednesday between two Thursdays or the Thursday between two Wednesdays, demonstrating the flexibility (tawassus) within Shia jurisprudence regarding the timing of the 'Ayyam al-Beed' or monthly Nafl fasts.
